title: JoyaGoo spreadsheet finds: how to shortlist the right listing
summary: A practical way to search by product type, compare two finds, read the selected option and carry the right marketplace link into JoyaGoo.

sections.heading: Start with what you can describe
paragraphs: Suppose you want the blue overshirt in a friend's photograph. You can see a straight hem, two square chest pockets and dark buttons. You cannot tell whether the fabric is cotton, what the seller called the colour, or what size your friend wore. Write down the first three details and leave the other three open. This small distinction changes the search. You have a way to recognise candidates, without excluding a promising find simply because its title calls it a work shirt or its photograph looks slightly grey.

On this site's Spreadsheet page, start with the shortest useful product name. Try “shirt” before a string such as “navy cotton men's long sleeve workwear overshirt with two chest pockets.” A long description works well in a message to a person. A catalogue may contain only a short title for the listing. Once you see the vocabulary used on plausible cards, borrow a word from those titles for your next query. Try “jacket” if the garment looks substantial and the shirt results are all dress shirts. Use the photo tool when you recognise the shape but cannot find a name for it.

sections.heading: Read the results page without losing your place
paragraphs: The range above the grid tells you which part of the current result set you are viewing. Category choices and search terms travel with the page links. The page-number field lets you go back to a particular part of a long list. If a search suddenly looks too narrow, look at the selected category as well as the words in the box. Searching inside shoes and searching across the entire catalogue can produce very different results for a term that also describes a piece of clothing.

Open promising items in separate tabs so that you can return to the same set of results. Save the product page when you spot a good candidate. A bookmark for page three of a search saves a position in a changing list. It offers little protection against the insertion of new products ahead of the one you liked. A direct product bookmark gives you a better starting point for the next visit. Keep the original seller link as well if the choice matters enough that you would contact the agent about it.

sections.heading: Work out what one unit buys
paragraphs: A product card has room for a name, a photograph and a reference price. The photograph may show an entire outfit, a row of colours or a pair of items displayed with accessories. Open the product and read the choices before comparing prices. A title that mentions a jacket and trousers might lead to separate upper and lower selections. Two photos can show both pieces even when a single selectable option purchases only one. Look for wording that describes the contents of the actual order line.

Consider two hypothetical listings for a matching outfit. One displays a higher card price and has an option explicitly described as a set. The other opens at a lower price with separate choices for the top and bottom. To compare them, select the pieces you need in each listing and record the total for the same outfit. If the second listing offers the same colour name for both pieces, look for photographs showing them together. If the contents of a set remain unclear after reading the selections, ask what is included before you pay.

sections.heading: Use two columns for competing finds
paragraphs: A useful comparison can fit on a phone screen. Give each candidate four lines in a note: the listing link, the option as written, the measurement or feature that matters, and the question still open. For the overshirt, you might record that candidate A has the right pocket arrangement but gives no sleeve length. Candidate B lists the sleeve measurement you need and shows a different cuff. You now have a specific choice between asking about A and accepting B's different construction.

Compare like with like. Lay a shirt you already wear on a flat surface and take the measurement you want to check. Record where you started and ended. If you measured across the flat chest, compare that with a flat chest width taken the same way. A circumference entry and a flat width may use similar labels while giving very different numbers. If the listing shows a diagram, follow its endpoints. A roomier cut can be intentional, so decide how you want the garment to fit before interpreting the difference.

sections.heading: Read the photographs in the order you need them
paragraphs: Start with the seller's option image to identify the design and colour offered. Move to the detail gallery to inspect features that the thumbnail hides. Then inspect any available QC photographs for a real example and check which option they show. A gallery for a listing with several variations may answer a construction question about one version while leaving the other versions undocumented. Save the image that supports your conclusion alongside the precise question it answered.

For the overshirt, a head-on picture might establish the placement of both chest pockets. A side picture might reveal a curved hem that was hidden when the model tucked in the shirt. Neither picture settles how long the sleeves will be on you. For that question, the relevant evidence is a measurement with visible endpoints. Notice how the next step changes with the uncertainty. Looking through ten more photographs of the front rarely helps with a missing measurement. A request for one specific measurement can move the decision forward.

sections.heading: Carry the listing and the variant together
paragraphs: When opening a find on JoyaGoo, compare the marketplace item with the one you just researched. Keep the seller listing address, check the selected colour and size, and reread the order line after you select them. An item number can identify the parent listing while several variants share it. Opening the same listing twice can still leave you with different styles selected. If you are sharing a find with someone else, include both the link and the exact option label, especially when the seller uses numbers in place of descriptive names.

JoyaGoo's official shopping guidance describes opening an original product link in its search field and choosing colour, size and quantity when placing an order. Use the original link as a second route if the buying link opens a generic view. If the marketplace listing has changed or the preferred choice has disappeared, keep the old reference for support and reconsider the purchase. A similarly titled result from another seller is a new candidate. Repeat the measurements and option check before treating it as a replacement.

sections.heading: Compare the price at the point where you can act
paragraphs: Pick one display currency while comparing products. Otherwise a tab left in one currency and another opened later can create an apparent price difference. On the agent's order page, inspect the selected variant, quantity, item charge and any local shipping shown. Record the time and currency beside the amount if you are sending your comparison to someone else. The separate question of sending a packed parcel overseas belongs in the parcel estimate and depends on the shipment you ultimately assemble.

Before you close the comparison, write one sentence explaining your choice. For example, “I chose the set that includes both pieces because its sleeve diagram matches my shirt, and I have saved the blue option label.” If you can only write “It looked closer in the thumbnail,” reopen the missing evidence. A shortlist has done its job when it lets you name the item, its seller listing, the variant you intend to buy and the reason you prefer it. You can then revisit the purchase without reconstructing an afternoon of browsing.

sources.title: JoyaGoo Sheet Hub — browse the spreadsheet

faqs.q: Where can I find a product again after the spreadsheet changes?
faqs.a: Bookmark its product detail page and save the original seller link with the chosen option. A catalogue page number can point to different products after new listings are added.

faqs.q: Does a JoyaGoo find showing a matching outfit include both pieces?
faqs.a: Read the selectable option and the order line. A single photograph can show a complete outfit while the seller offers the top, bottom and full set as separate choices.

faqs.q: How can I compare spreadsheet prices for two product variants?
faqs.a: Use one display currency and select the same size, quantity and contents for each candidate. Confirm each item amount and domestic delivery charge in JoyaGoo before comparing totals.

title: JoyaGoo image search: find a listing from a product photo
summary: Choose a useful crop, interpret changing photo matches and distinguish a visually similar find from the exact seller listing and variant.

sections.heading: Choose the question your photograph can answer
paragraphs: There are two quite different searches behind the phrase “find this by photo.” One person has lost a listing and wants to recover a photograph they remember seeing. Another saw a bag on a train and wants something with the same shape and strap. For the first person, tiny details such as the direction of a crease or the position of a handle can establish that two pages use the same photograph. For the second, the size of the bag opening and whether the strap detaches may be more important than finding a duplicate image.

Make that decision before opening the camera button. If you want the same listing, retain the original screenshot and any visible seller or item information. A store name or a fragment of a product title may become useful later. If you want a similar design, write down the features you need the product to have independent of its presentation. A pleasant shade of green under warm lighting is a weak requirement. A crossbody bag with a short top handle and a zip opening is a description you can test against the gallery.

sections.heading: Give the search one object to compare
paragraphs: A screenshot of a shopping page contains several kinds of information. A banner, a row of tiny swatches, a portrait of a model and the phone's navigation controls may surround the product photograph. Save the original, then crop a copy around the photograph you want to compare. Include the whole outline of the object when it fits comfortably in the frame. If a shoulder bag has a distinctive strap attachment, keep the attachment visible even if the rest of the strap extends beyond the crop.

For a collage, crop one panel at a time. The front of a shoe photographed against a white background makes one query. Its outsole photographed against a grey floor makes another. Combining the panels gives the search a pattern of rectangles and backgrounds that may be absent from every individual seller photo. Conversely, if your goal is to recover the very same collage and you know the listing used one, try the intact image first. Choose the crop according to the image you expect to find, then change one thing if it fails.

sections.heading: Start the search and read the counters
paragraphs: Open Image search in the navigation or use the camera beside the search field. Choose a photo saved on your device. On a browser that supplies image data through the clipboard, you can also paste a copied image into the search page. An image copied as a URL is text, so save the actual picture or copy the image itself if pasting a link does nothing. The preview is a useful first check. It shows which file is being compared, an easy thing to overlook when several screenshots have similar file names.

Result cards can change as additional products are checked. The page counts photos and products separately because a single listing can supply multiple views. It first compares the available indexed images and then checks for additional images from current listings. During that second pass, the product counter can start over while existing matches remain on screen. If you see a promising card, open it in another tab. The pause control lets you inspect a set of candidates without asking the search to start over with the same photograph.

sections.heading: Why a close result can show the wrong product
paragraphs: The matcher on this site compares the distribution of colour and the arrangement of light and dark areas across the picture. A dark square bag centred on a pale table and a dark rectangular pouch photographed on a similar table can look surprisingly close at that scale. The search does not read a logo, inspect a product code or identify a seller from the photograph. Those pieces of evidence become available when you open a result and examine the listing for yourself.

Picture a green bag shown against a red chair. If your first results mostly contain red furniture or reddish backgrounds, crop more of the chair away while preserving the bag's shape. A very tight crop of green fabric may go too far in the opposite direction. It removes the outline, handle and fastening that distinguish a bag from a jacket. Compare the two sets of results and keep the crop that brings back objects of the right type. Move to a second angle if changing the crop merely produces different green textures.

sections.heading: Inspect the matched picture before the cover
paragraphs: Each result card shows the image that earned that listing its place. A product may match through a detail picture or a style image even when the cover looks different. Open the result and inspect the matching view alongside the rest of the gallery. A close match to a strap buckle might be a useful starting point for the bag search. It will take an overall photograph to tell whether the buckle belongs to a shoulder bag, a belt or a separate strap sold on its own.

Now look for a second, independent feature. With a bag, compare the number of seams around the base, where the side rings attach, or whether the zipper continues down the sides. For a shoe, inspect the shape of the outsole edge from the same angle or the position of a panel relative to the eyelets. If the details differ, record the result as a similar design. If they agree, check the available measurements and material descriptions. The strongest visual candidate still needs to satisfy the practical reason you wanted it.

sections.heading: Recover a listing when several sellers share a photo
paragraphs: Finding the identical photograph solves an image question. Recovering the seller requires something else, because different listings can use the same promotional image. Reopen your uncropped screenshot and look for the marketplace, a partial product number, a store name or a distinctive written option. A shared crease, shadow and camera angle are evidence that you found the picture. Matching the marketplace and original listing address gives you a much stronger basis for saying that you found the seller's listing again.

If two candidates remain, send their original listing links to the person who supplied the photo and ask which one they used. If you cannot recover that information, treat the candidates as separate offers. One may sell a strap alone while the other includes the pictured bag. One may still offer the colour you want and the other may only display its photograph in the gallery. Compare the actual contents, size and current selection on JoyaGoo before paying. Putting a familiar photograph in a cart has little value if the order line describes something else.

sections.heading: Diagnose an empty or interrupted search
paragraphs: Look at the preview, status and cards separately. A missing preview suggests that the selected image could not be read. Save a fresh copy in a common format such as JPEG or PNG and select it again. A visible preview with a growing product count shows that comparisons are running. An unavailable count or an interruption can indicate that some images or results could not be fetched. Retrying with a working connection tests that possibility. A completed search with no close matches calls for a different picture or a different search method.

Keep one alternative route in reserve. For a lost link, a readable item number or the original listing in your message history is a better lead than repeatedly cropping the same low-resolution thumbnail. For a similar design, take terms from the best-looking candidates and enter them in the spreadsheet's text search. A third route is the official JoyaGoo product search, which its shopping guidance describes as accepting a product name, photo or original link. Choose the route that uses the most specific information you still have. The goal is a listing you can verify and an option you can select with confidence.

sources.title: JoyaGoo Sheet Hub — search by image

faqs.q: Can I paste a product photo into JoyaGoo Sheet Hub image search?
faqs.a: Yes, when your browser copies the image itself to the clipboard. If you copied a web address, save the picture and select it using Choose a photo instead.

faqs.q: Why does a photo search show a different picture from the listing cover?
faqs.a: The result displays the matching image for that product. A style, detail or gallery photo can be closer to your query than the seller’s cover photograph.

faqs.q: Can an exact image match identify the original Weidian seller?
faqs.a: Several sellers may reuse the same photograph. Compare the marketplace item number and original listing URL with your saved reference, then verify the selected style on the live listing.

title: How to Buy on JoyaGoo with a Weidian or Taobao Product Link
summary: Follow one listing from a spreadsheet find to an item order and an international parcel. Check the seller, selected options and first payment before the agent purchases it.

sections.heading: Start with the link you would give someone looking for the same item
paragraphs: Suppose a friend sends you a picture of a green zip pouch and a Weidian link. Open the link before using the picture to search. Does it lead to one product with selectable options, or to a shop with several similar pouches? A product link gives JoyaGoo a particular listing to look up. A photograph gives you a way to find candidates. Keep both while you shop. The link can tell you where to place the order, and the picture can tell you whether you have opened the intended design.

If you found the pouch in the JoyaGoo spreadsheet, open its detail page and look for the buying link. You can follow that link directly when it opens the right JoyaGoo listing. If you are starting on a marketplace instead, use the share option for the individual item and paste its link into the product search on JoyaGoo. Give the page time to display its options, then compare it with the original. A home page, image file, shopping cart or social post leaves the seller or the item ambiguous.

sections.heading: Check what the seller is offering
paragraphs: Read the words beside the product options even if the main photo looks familiar. A desk organiser pictured with six drawers may be sold as one drawer, a set or a replacement insert. A low starting price makes sense for the insert and says little about the full organiser. Click the option you actually want and read its price again. Look for a unit such as piece, pair, set or pack. If the unit is unclear in translation, save the original wording and ask what one order contains.

Use details that are hard to mistake. For the green pouch, compare the zipper placement, the number of compartments and the size against the original listing. Another seller can use the same promotional photograph. A matching photo on its own will lead you astray if the second seller offers only a smaller version. Keep the original marketplace name, seller name where visible and product link together. If you reopen the find in a different language later, those references are more dependable than a translated product title.

sections.heading: Carry the selection into the cart
paragraphs: Choose each required option and set the quantity. On a listing that groups several designs under one product, selecting the colour can change which sizes or configurations you can buy. After the last selection, look back through the selected labels. Open the cart and read the actual line item. If the cart says green, small, one piece while the listing photograph shows two matching pouches, decide whether one small pouch is what you meant to order.

Suppose you want two green pouches and one navy pouch from the same seller. Add the green selection with a quantity of two. Return to the listing and add the navy selection with a quantity of one. In the cart you should be able to account for three units and both colours before paying. A note that says “one navy” alongside a cart line for three green pieces leaves two competing instructions. Resolve the selection in the cart whenever the normal options allow it.

sections.heading: Read the first payment as an item purchase
paragraphs: JoyaGoo's buying guide describes an initial payment for the goods and Chinese domestic shipping. The seller's delivery leg ends at the warehouse. International delivery to your address is a later decision. Look at the currency and the amount due at the point of payment, especially if you have been browsing the spreadsheet in a different display currency. Keep a copy of the checkout details so you can tell later which part of the journey a charge belongs to.

A simple budget can start with three entries on a piece of paper: goods, seller-to-warehouse delivery and warehouse-to-home delivery. Write a figure beside an entry only when you know what it covers. If the seller offers local delivery at no charge, record that against the domestic entry and leave the international figure open. For an inexpensive bulky item, it is worth checking available shipping estimates before buying. A large empty organiser takes up space in a parcel even when the contents weigh very little.

sections.heading: When the link opens the wrong page or produces no result
paragraphs: Go back to the original product and copy the individual listing again. Check that the shared text actually contains the link, rather than just a title or a picture. Open the original to see whether the seller still offers the item and variant. If the original now leads to a shop home page or an unavailable product, a fresh copy of the same address may lead to the same place. An old cart screenshot can establish what you wanted, but it cannot establish current stock.

JoyaGoo describes a DIY order route for products its ordinary search cannot retrieve. If that route is available for your listing, give the agent a specific request: the source link, the option names as the seller writes them, the unit and the count. Add an image showing the selected configuration when words alone could mean two things. For a listing with an unclear price, a deposit or several possible sellers, ask for the purchase terms before paying. Supplying a photo does not establish that a seller has agreed to supply that exact configuration at the displayed amount.

sections.heading: Follow the order through arrival at the warehouse
paragraphs: Once you have placed the order, use the order record in your JoyaGoo account to track what happens next. An agent order number identifies your purchase request. A seller's local shipment and your eventual international parcel refer to different movements of goods. A domestic delivery update is a reason to check the order again, while the overseas carrier will become relevant after you submit goods for international dispatch. Keeping those references in separately named notes saves confusion when several products arrive on different days.

Compare the warehouse images for your order with what you chose at checkout. For the pouch, a label or dimension may separate the small and large versions more clearly than a front view. If the photos show the wrong colour or an unexpected quantity, keep the item at the warehouse while asking about your options. Include the order reference, the selected option and the photo that shows the difference. That is easier for someone to investigate than a message saying the product looks different. Use the live terms on your order for any return or exchange decision.

sections.heading: Make the parcel decision separately
paragraphs: When the goods you want to send are ready, review the items and address on the parcel submission. Compare eligible delivery options for that parcel and destination. Check which amount is an estimate, what extra packing you selected and what the final payment covers. If one item is still being resolved with the seller, decide whether the other items should travel without it. A single seller purchase can lead to several parcel decisions, and purchases placed on separate days can arrive at the warehouse at different times.

Before leaving the order screen, save enough information to answer three practical questions later. Which listing did I choose? Which option did I pay for? Which parcel contains the goods? For a single pouch this can fit on one line with links to the order and parcel. For a shared household order, record the colour and quantity beside each person's name. If a parcel arrives with one navy pouch and two green ones, you can account for the contents without trying to reconstruct the original request from a gallery of similar photographs.

sources.title: JoyaGoo Help Center — Shipping Products Purchased at Different Times

faqs.q: Where do I paste a Weidian or Taobao link on JoyaGoo?
faqs.a: Copy the individual marketplace product link into the official JoyaGoo product search. Compare the seller, item and options on the resulting listing before adding it to the cart.

faqs.q: Does the first JoyaGoo payment cover international shipping?
faqs.a: The initial order covers the merchandise and applicable Chinese domestic delivery. Review international delivery separately when submitting goods from the warehouse as a parcel.

faqs.q: What can I do when JoyaGoo cannot read my product link?
faqs.a: Reopen the original listing and copy its individual product URL. When standard search cannot retrieve it, JoyaGoo documents a DIY order option. Supply the exact version, seller link, quantity and price details you can verify.

title: JoyaGoo Size Guide: Read a Seller’s Size Chart and Choose the Right Variant
summary: Use a garment you own to compare two sizes, identify which option changes the fit and ask for a measurement that settles a specific question.

sections.heading: Choose something you already own as a reference
paragraphs: A favourite sweatshirt can answer a question that a letter on a label cannot. Take one out of the cupboard that you actually like wearing over the layer you have in mind. Lay it on a flat surface, let the fabric settle and measure it without stretching the knit. Write down where you put each end of the tape. The next time you compare an unfamiliar seller's sweatshirt with yours, you will have a repeatable starting point even if the two labels use different sizing systems.

Pick a reference with a similar job. A slim T-shirt makes a poor starting point for a jacket you want to wear over a hoodie. For trousers, choose a pair that sits at the height you like and feels right when you sit down. If you are shopping for someone else, ask for measurements of a garment they are happy to lend or measure themselves. “The blue shirt you like measures this much across the chest” gives you something specific to compare with a seller's chart.

sections.heading: Identify what the size chart measures
paragraphs: Look for the unit, the diagram and the words attached to the numbers. Some charts describe the body of the intended wearer. Others describe the finished garment laid out on a table. A chest number means something different in each case. A diagram with a line from one underarm to the other is measuring a width. A line going around the wearer represents a circumference. If a listing gives a number but omits the diagram and description, ask which measurement the seller used.

Consider a made-up example. Your sweatshirt is 54 cm wide under the arms. A seller lists a finished chest circumference of 108 cm. Under the same measuring method, doubling a flat width of 54 cm gives a perimeter of about 108 cm. If the seller's 108 cm instead refers to the wearer's chest, the calculation tells you nothing about the actual width of the sweatshirt. Resolve the meaning of the column before comparing rows. UNIQLO's measurement guide illustrates this distinction for its own clothing. Another seller's diagram remains the authority for that seller's item.

sections.heading: Compare the dimensions that affect how you wear the item
paragraphs: For a shirt with a conventional shoulder seam, start with chest width, back length and the shoulder span the chart specifies. If you tuck your shirts in, length may matter as much as chest room. If you wear them open over a thick T-shirt, check the chest and upper sleeve before concentrating on the hem. For a dropped-shoulder or raglan sleeve, look carefully for the stated starting point. A sleeve measured from the neck includes a section that is missing from a sleeve measured from the shoulder seam.

Trousers need a different comparison. Lay your reference pair flat with the waistband fastened if that matches the diagram. Record the relaxed waistband, rise and inseam. If the waistband is elastic, separate its resting width from any stretched measurement the seller supplies. Two pairs can share an inseam and still hang differently when the rise changes. Compare the thigh if that is where your reference pair feels tight. A chart can show you a likely trade-off before you buy, even when two adjacent sizes would both fit at the waist.

sections.heading: Work through two plausible sizes
paragraphs: Imagine your reference shirt measures 53 cm across the chest and 69 cm down the back. A seller's comparison table gives one shirt as 52 by 69 and the next as 55 by 72, using the same garment measurements. The smaller row is close in length and narrower across the chest. The larger row adds width and three centimetres of length. If you need the shirt for a uniform with a fixed hem position, your choice could differ from that of someone wearing it open as an overshirt.

To see whether a difference matters, move the tape from 69 to 72 cm along your reference shirt. You can see where the longer hem would end. Try the reference shirt over your planned layer and notice where the extra width would be welcome. This exercise can also help you leave a listing behind. If you want more chest room while keeping a short hem and neither row offers that shape, another cut may meet both needs more comfortably than a compromise on size.

sections.heading: Decode colour, material and version options
paragraphs: On a marketplace listing, the option translated as “colour” can carry more information than a shade. Read every part of the chosen label and compare its picture with the description. Two black jackets might be offered on the same page, one lined and one unlined. A thumbnail showing the back of a jacket might identify a design rather than a colour change. Switch between the choices and look for differences in the words, pictures, available sizes and price. Save the combination that you want before you leave the listing.

For a multi-piece outfit, establish whether your chosen option buys the top, the trousers or the set. Then check whether a set lets you choose different sizes for the two pieces. An image of a complete outfit cannot answer either question. For a bag, identify whether dimensions refer to the bag itself or the length of its strap. If you need the bag to hold a particular object, the width of the opening and the usable interior matter more than the outside diagonal. Ask for the missing dimension while another option is still easy to choose.

sections.heading: Ask for one measurement that could change your decision
paragraphs: When the listing leaves a meaningful gap, make your question easy to answer. A buyer comparing two jackets could ask for the finished back length of the lined black jacket in medium, measured from the base of the collar to the hem. Include the original option label or a marked picture if two black versions appear side by side. That question identifies one item, two endpoints and one unit. A generic request for a size recommendation requires the other person to guess both your preferred fit and what you already know.

JoyaGoo lists a detailed-photo service that can include measurements. Check the option and price shown for your order before requesting it. Describe what you would like the photo to show, such as the jacket laid flat and the tape visible from the first endpoint to the second. A cropped photograph of a number at the hem is hard to interpret if you cannot see where the tape started. A measurement taken after storage is especially valuable when it would influence your decision to ship or contact support. It cannot retroactively settle a seller's return conditions.

sections.heading: Record the choice that should arrive
paragraphs: Before paying, read the final option line in JoyaGoo. Compare the size, colour, version and quantity with the combination you chose on the seller's page. Save the chart or screenshot together with the order details, especially if a seller uses one listing for several seasons or cuts. A screenshot that includes the relevant row, units and column headings is worth more than a crop containing only the letter M. When buying two sizes, keep their order lines separate so you can match each delivered piece with the right expectation.

After the item arrives at the warehouse, start with the easiest observable checks. Read the label where it is visible. Compare the selected option's details with the piece in your order photos. If fit depends on a measurement, compare the actual piece with your reference garment using the same endpoints. Ask about a visible discrepancy before submitting the parcel. If every number matches but you dislike the cut, record that distinction for your next purchase. You now know which dimension you would change, and can use that knowledge on the next seller's chart.

sources.title: JoyaGoo Help Center — Value Added Services

faqs.q: Can I use my usual letter size for every JoyaGoo listing?
faqs.a: Check the specific seller’s chart and cut. Compare the garment dimensions with a similar piece you like, or use body measurements when the chart explicitly gives wearer dimensions.

faqs.q: How do I compare a flat chest width with a chest circumference?
faqs.a: First confirm both numbers describe the finished garment at the same point. Under those conditions, twice the flat width approximates its circumference. A body chest measurement requires a chart designed for body measurements.

faqs.q: Can I request a JoyaGoo warehouse photo with a measuring tape?
faqs.a: JoyaGoo lists detailed photographs with measurements as an optional service. Name the item, specify both endpoints and request a visible tape in your preferred unit. Check the option and current fee in your order.

title: How to read JoyaGoo QC photos and request a useful measurement
summary: Find the photos for your own order, compare the right variant, and give the warehouse precise instructions for the one detail you still need.

sections.heading: Find the photo set attached to your order
paragraphs: A seller can photograph a navy jacket so that it looks black. A warehouse can do the same under a different light. Before opening a dispute about color, look for a detail that will settle the question without relying on a screen. A readable color code on a hangtag, for example, may answer it in seconds. That habit of choosing evidence to fit the question makes a JoyaGoo QC review considerably more useful than scrolling through a gallery looking for something wrong.

Start in the order section of your JoyaGoo account. Open the entry for the particular item and look for the completed warehouse inspection. JoyaGoo's shopping guide explains that stock arrival and QC completion are separate steps. If you only see the seller's dispatch information, return to the order after the warehouse records the inspection. Keep the order number and variant text visible beside the photos, especially if you bought two sizes of the same garment. A spreadsheet gallery can help you recognize a design, but you need the pictures attached to this purchase to decide what to send home.

sections.heading: Read the overview before zooming in
paragraphs: Imagine you ordered a jacket with a detachable hood. One warehouse picture shows the front zipped up and another shows the back, with fabric folded over the neck. Zooming into the fold will never tell you whether the hood is attached. Look for a second view of the neckline and for any separate piece lying next to the jacket. Then reread the listing option you paid for. A hood pictured on the first product card might belong to a different option in the same listing. This is a question about what was included, which an overview can often resolve.

On that first pass, count the pieces you can actually see. For shoes, look for both feet and check any visible labels on the pair. For a bundle, compare the names of the included pieces with the objects in the frame. A listing sold by the piece can use a photograph styled as a complete outfit. If a belt appears in a seller photo but the purchased option says trousers only, the difference starts in the listing description. If the paid option explicitly includes the belt, ask for a picture showing it beside the trousers.

sections.heading: Make a flat measurement comparable
paragraphs: For a shirt, take out a shirt that already fits you the way you want. Button it, smooth it on a flat surface and measure straight across the front between the two points where the sleeves meet the side seams. Write down the distance and units. You now have a reproducible target for a warehouse request. A body measurement taken around your chest describes a different thing. Comparing that number directly with the width of a flat shirt produces a dramatic apparent discrepancy even when the garment is exactly the expected size.

Here is a practical request for a stored item. “For item [number], please lay the shirt flat with the buttons closed. Measure straight across between the underarm seams in centimetres. Please include both tape ends and both seams in one overhead photo.” The item number identifies the shirt, the landmarks define the line, and the view lets you read the result yourself. If one end is tucked under the sleeve or the first visible mark is several centimetres along the tape, ask for that point to be made visible. A sharp image of a misplaced tape still gives the wrong answer.

Trouser measurements need a different description. A waistband can be measured with the front fastened and lying relaxed. An inseam follows the inside of the leg from the crotch seam to the hem. For each, tell the photographer which end points you used on your own garment. If the seller chart lists a range for an elastic waist, a single relaxed width only answers one part of the question. Avoid asking staff to stretch delicate fabric to its limit. Compare the relaxed measurements first and ask the seller to explain what its chart represents.

sections.heading: Decide when to ask for a retake
paragraphs: An unreadable standard photo and a missing custom view have different remedies. JoyaGoo's detailed photo instructions say that a shopper may request a free retake of an unclear standard image. The same instructions describe a paid service for special angles, close-ups and measurements. If blur hides the label already featured in the standard picture, identify the photo and ask for a sharper version. If you want the inside label photographed when it was never part of that view, open the detailed photo option and check the current charge before submitting.

Give each requested picture a purpose. For a backpack, an overall view of the straps could establish whether both buckles are present. A close-up of a particular strap attachment could show a visible tear. Asking for ten more angles of the whole backpack is unlikely to resolve a question about one seam. You might describe the spot as “the attachment of the left shoulder strap, viewed from the back with the carry handle at the top.” That description still makes sense if the receiving staff member has never seen your drawing or highlighted screenshot.

sections.heading: Interpret folds, shadows and surface marks
paragraphs: A dark line running across a sleeve may follow the fabric's fold. Find the same spot in a second image, using the cuff button or a seam as your reference. If the line appears to move with the fold, request a photograph with the sleeve smoothed and the area uncovered. If both images show the same break in the same stitching, you can describe the exact location to the agent. Keep the untouched original along with any cropped copy. An annotated crop is easiest to understand when the recipient can also see which sleeve you mean.

JoyaGoo describes the standard inspection as an external visual check. That matters when deciding what to do with an otherwise reassuring image. A photo of a digital accessory can establish which connector is visible on its case. It cannot establish battery capacity, power-on behavior or compatibility with your particular device. Similarly, a picture of a shoe can capture its marked size and an outsole measurement. Neither detail tells you how much usable room is inside the toe box. Ask for evidence the photographer can actually collect, then decide whether the remaining uncertainty is acceptable for that purchase.

sections.heading: Close the review while a choice is still available
paragraphs: Suppose the jacket's hangtag matches your chosen variant, the chest measurement matches your comparison jacket, and the remaining concern is a pale patch near a pocket. The single most useful next image is a clear view of that pocket with the fabric smooth. Give the item number and explain where you see the patch. While waiting, check the return option and the time recorded for the completed QC. JoyaGoo publishes a limited return period for eligible warehouse purchases. A request for another photo should never be your only action when that deadline is approaching.

Keep a brief record of what you decided and why. A note saying “pocket reviewed in the follow-up image, dimensions checked against the blue jacket” is more useful than a row of unlabeled screenshots. If you accepted a slight shade difference, you can later distinguish it from an unrelated shipping issue. If you requested an exchange, keep the original order and photo reference with the replacement details. When another item arrives, assess that new item on its own photos before sending it with the rest of the parcel.

sources.title: How JoyaGoo handles visible quality issues

faqs.q: Where are the QC photos for my own JoyaGoo purchase?
faqs.a: Open the item in your JoyaGoo order history after its warehouse inspection is complete. Match the order number and selected variant before reviewing the photos.

faqs.q: Can I request a clearer JoyaGoo QC picture?
faqs.a: JoyaGoo describes a free retake for an unclear standard photo. For a new angle or a specific measurement, select the detailed photo service and check the charge shown in your account.

faqs.q: How should I ask JoyaGoo to measure a shirt?
faqs.a: Give the warehouse item number and ask for a flat, buttoned shirt measured straight between the underarm seams. Specify centimetres and request a photo that shows the tape start, tape end and both seams.

title: JoyaGoo warehouse returns and exchanges before international shipping
summary: Use the QC timestamp, paid variant and seller conditions to choose a remedy, submit the request and check the resulting refund or replacement.

sections.heading: Find the deadline for the individual item
paragraphs: You open your warehouse list and notice that one of two shirts is the wrong size. The other shirt is ready and you had planned to send them together. Leave the questionable shirt out of the parcel while you check the order. Your first two questions are which size the paid order shows and when its warehouse inspection finished. The time you first saw the photo may be quite different. JoyaGoo's return policy gives eligible orders a window of five days, expressed as 120 hours, from the change to “QC completed.”

Read the time on that individual order and any deadline the account displays. If two purchases reached the warehouse on different days, each needs its own check. Suppose a QC entry is recorded at noon on Monday and you first look at it on Thursday evening. In this example much of the window has already passed. Preserve the time zone shown on the order if you share the timestamp with support. Do not use a storage expiry date to calculate when you can return an item. Storage covers the time it can stay in the building, and a seller return follows a separate timetable.

sections.heading: Establish what the seller was asked to supply
paragraphs: Open the exact purchased variant, then put the QC photo beside a screenshot of that order line. The listing's default selection today may differ from the option you chose yesterday. For a bundle, read the pieces included in the option. For clothing, compare the tag with the ordered size and use the seller's chart for that item. If you ordered a medium, the label says medium and the cut is closer than you expected, describe a fit preference. If the label says small and your receipt records medium, describe the mismatch directly.

Consider a jacket with two versions, one lined and one unlined. A jacket that looks padded on the seller's cover image may still be the unlined version you bought. Inspect the option text and the actual lining visible in the warehouse photos. When the paid version is clear but the interior is hidden, identify the missing view and request it promptly. If the order is near its deadline, contact the agent about the after-sales request while that evidence is being gathered. A general question about the lining leaves the agent guessing whether you actually want a remedy.

sections.heading: Match the remedy to the problem
paragraphs: An exchange makes sense when you still want this exact listing and can identify a suitable replacement. Provide the target variant precisely. A size name, a color, the seller's option code and any price difference may all matter. Check availability again because another buyer may have bought the replacement in the meantime. Say what the agent should do if the variant is unavailable. Asking to be contacted first leaves the final choice with you and avoids having the seller substitute a related color or an adjacent size without your agreement.

A return is easier to describe when the listing itself no longer meets your needs. Perhaps the seller confirmed that even the largest size uses the same short sleeve length. Exchanging for the next size would move the stock around without addressing that concern. Check the eligibility and costs the account shows for your purchase. JoyaGoo's policy requires the item to meet the seller's resale conditions. Its published exclusions include personalized goods and some items with removed packaging or tags. If special packaging matters, leave it intact while the seller reviews your case.

sections.heading: Send a request another person can act on
paragraphs: Use the return or exchange control beside the affected order in your account, where available. Include the order identifier, the ordered variant, what the evidence shows and your requested outcome. For example, “My order shows the blue shirt in medium. The collar tag in the second warehouse photo reads small. Please request an exchange for blue in medium. If it is unavailable, please tell me the return cost before proceeding.” This gives the agent both a specific instruction and a boundary for the alternative. Copying a complete product title into the message rarely adds the same clarity.

For visible damage, keep your words as narrow as your evidence. “There is a split at the side seam below the right pocket in this picture” tells the seller what to inspect. “Everything is defective” gives the seller little to evaluate, particularly if you ordered several items. Include a wider view as well as a close crop so that the location can be recognized. If the product falls outside the standard return guarantee, the official policy directs quality concerns to seller review. Include the relevant facts and wait for an actual decision before assuming the item qualifies.

sections.heading: Check the costs and the status record
paragraphs: Read any quoted domestic postage and service charge before confirming. JoyaGoo's policy distinguishes a documented quality issue from a change of mind when discussing who bears return shipping. Keep the reason accurate and check what the agent and seller agree for this order. A headline about a return guarantee alone is an inadequate budget for an exchange. The new variant could have a different price, and the replacement could arrive separately from items already waiting. Ask about the amount shown in your account if it is unclear which part it covers.

The status in your order history helps distinguish a submitted case from a completed one. JoyaGoo's order-status guide describes “Returning” as the stage when goods have been sent back and the refund is still outstanding. It describes “Returned” as completion with the refund recorded in the account balance. Look at the relevant balance entry when you reconcile the result. Record the price actually paid for the item and compare it with the credited amount and the fees agreed. If they differ, send the order ID, the original charged amount and the specific balance transaction to the agent.

sections.heading: Handle the rest of the parcel separately
paragraphs: An exchange affects the timing of other items only if you decide to wait for it. Look at the storage dates and the shipping estimates for the pieces you already have. A replacement may be worth waiting for when you have plenty of time and need both pieces as a set. If the remaining items have an earlier storage deadline, ask what your options are before leaving them all untouched. The cost of sending two parcels needs a fresh quote for each group. Dividing an earlier total in half tells you very little about the actual options.

When the replacement appears, use its own warehouse images to check the point that prompted the exchange. In the blue-shirt example, look for the new collar tag and the chosen color together. A photograph of the outside packet alone might repeat the seller's option description without showing the garment inside. Keep the original and replacement photos under different filenames so a later question can be answered without reopening the entire conversation. Once the new item satisfies the original concern, you can make a shipping decision using the current warehouse list and the current parcel quote.

sections.heading: If the return control has disappeared
paragraphs: First make sure you opened the order for the item itself and check its QC timestamp. If the control has expired or the item has special conditions, contact JoyaGoo through the account with the order details and describe any genuine unresolved issue. Ask whether the agent can consult the seller and whether the item is still available to inspect. Record the response. A warehouse request and a problem discovered after international delivery involve different circumstances. If a parcel has already left, tell support its actual status so that it can direct you to the appropriate process.

faqs.q: When does the JoyaGoo warehouse return window begin?
faqs.a: For eligible items JoyaGoo publishes a 120-hour window starting when the order reaches QC completed. Check the timestamp and return control on the individual purchase.

faqs.q: What details should I give for a JoyaGoo exchange?
faqs.a: Identify the order, the discrepancy or reason, and the exact replacement size and color. Ask the agent to confirm availability and any costs before agreeing to a substitute.

faqs.q: Where does a completed JoyaGoo return refund appear?
faqs.a: JoyaGoo defines Returned as a completed refund to the account balance. While an order shows Returning, the refund is still pending. Compare the balance entry with your order and agreed charges.

title: JoyaGoo shipping cost explained with a worked volumetric weight example
summary: Compare two shipping lines using the same parcel, calculate when carton size changes the bill, and trace a difference between an estimate and the final freight charge.

sections.heading: Start with the box you intend to send
paragraphs: A two-kilogram pair of shoes and a two-kilogram winter coat can produce very different shipping estimates. Picture the shoes in a close-fitting carton and the coat in a much taller one. A scale records the same weight, while an airline has to find rather different amounts of room for the boxes. Before asking how much JoyaGoo charges per kilogram, find out which measurement the available shipping line uses for your particular parcel. That single detail determines whether another weighing or another measurement will improve your estimate.

Make a short note of the destination, items, packaging you intend to retain and the currency shown beside the price. For an item still in the shopping cart, write “estimated” beside the dimensions. For one in the warehouse, note whether the figures describe an individual item in its retail packaging or a parcel that has already been packed. A product-page measurement can refer to a garment laid flat. Entering that as the length of the shipping carton gives a perfectly precise answer to the wrong question.

sections.heading: Read the units before comparing lines
paragraphs: Actual packed weight includes everything that will cross the scale together. That includes the carton and any protective material. Volumetric weight converts the external space taken up by that carton into a weight for billing. For a line that compares the two, the larger figure determines the starting weight for the price calculation. JoyaGoo publishes examples of different divisors and line-specific conditions. Some conditions depend on the length of a side. Read the rule attached to the line offered for your destination each time you compare prices.

Write the three outer dimensions in centimetres in one row, even if two sides have the same measurement. Multiply length by width by height, then divide by the divisor specified for the selected route. When the formula uses centimetres and gives kilograms, compare the answer with the scale reading in kilograms. Convert a reading in grams by dividing by one thousand. Keep the unrounded answer in the note. Apply any published billing increment in a separate step so you can see how much of the difference came from rounding.

sections.heading: Work one parcel through two rules
paragraphs: Take a hypothetical carton measuring 42 by 30 by 20 centimetres, with a packed scale weight of 3.4 kilograms. The volume is 25,200 cubic centimetres. With a divisor of 6,000, the volumetric result is 4.2 kilograms. With a divisor of 5,000, the same box comes to 5.04 kilograms. If both hypothetical lines charge on the larger weight, their starting figures are 4.2 and 5.04 kilograms respectively. No shipping price follows from that arithmetic until you also know the applicable rate and billing steps.

A second calculation can tell you which measurement is worth refining. Imagine the warehouse can safely reduce the height to 16 centimetres while the other sides and the scale reading stay the same. With the 6,000 divisor the result becomes 3.36 kilograms. On the hypothetical greater-weight line, the scale reading of 3.4 kilograms would now count. Compressing the carton further would have no effect on that comparison unless the scale weight also changed. These are example measurements for learning the calculation. Only the warehouse can confirm a workable packed size for your goods.

sections.heading: Capture comparable quotes in one sitting
paragraphs: Open the official estimate with the destination and product category you intend to use. Take the first eligible line and record its name exactly as shown, the amount, currency, dimensions, scale weight, and which services the amount includes. Leave an empty space for anything the checkout has yet to price. Run the same inputs on the next line. If you alter both the route and the carton size at the same time, a cheaper result cannot tell you whether the saving came from packing or the tariff.

Suppose the first quote includes an optional service and the second omits it. Look up the cost of that service on the second line if you need it, or remove it from the first comparison if it is optional and you would decline it. If one route excludes your item, cross out that route even when its headline price looks attractive. Do the comparison in the currency displayed throughout. A converted amount on a spreadsheet is convenient for planning, while the currency and amount in your payment screen give you a precise figure to record.

sections.heading: Test the parcel against the decision you actually face
paragraphs: If you are deciding whether to add a sweatshirt, run the existing parcel and the combined parcel as two scenarios on the same line. The difference between their quotes is the estimated extra freight associated with adding it. Dividing the starting quote by the number of items answers another question entirely. It assigns an average share to every item, including the lightest one. Use the incremental figure for the buying decision and use an explicitly agreed allocation if you later split a parcel bill with someone else.

Allow for the shape change. A folded sweatshirt might fit into existing space, or its addition might require a deeper carton. When no packed measurements exist yet, try both plausible heights and save both outcomes as estimates. Avoid describing either amount as a warehouse quote. If the decision changes between those outcomes, you have learned something useful about the uncertainty. Getting the packed dimensions could determine whether to send those items together. If both outcomes are comfortably acceptable, an approximate figure may already answer the question you came to ask.

sections.heading: Separate freight from the rest of the order
paragraphs: Read the receipt heading before adding an amount to your comparison. The item purchase and transport from the seller to the Chinese warehouse belong to an earlier stage. International freight covers the parcel submitted from the warehouse. Extra photos, packing requests or insurance may appear as separate choices. Make a line for each actual charge and mark whether you have already paid it. For a comparison between routes, keep costs already incurred on their own line so they cannot accidentally appear as a saving when you switch routes.

Consider a familiar budgeting mistake. You set aside a total for the whole order, look at a shipping estimate and then compare that estimate with the full amount left on a payment card. The comparison looks comfortable until you remember that another item in the parcel still has an unpaid charge. A simple two-column note, paid and still to pay, avoids that confusion. Record unknown amounts as unknown. A blank cell treated as zero can make a route look affordable even when the actual figure is still missing.

sections.heading: Reconcile the amount after the warehouse packs
paragraphs: JoyaGoo describes the initial billing figure as an estimate based on the stored goods and anticipated packing. Packing produces new measurements, and the logistics provider can also revise a measurement. If a figure changes, open the parcel record and compare the selected items, route name, external dimensions and packed weight with the original note. Then calculate the volumetric result under the same rule. If you jump straight from two different totals to a complaint about the price per kilogram, you can overlook a larger carton or a different route.

For a question about a specific parcel, send the parcel reference and the two sets of figures through the official account support channel. State the difference you want explained in one sentence. For instance, you might ask which carton height was used when the billed weight changed, or whether a higher total includes a packing service listed separately on the earlier screen. Keep the dated quote and the final parcel record together. On a future order, your best reference will be a parcel with similar contents, destination, packaging and route terms.

sources.title: JoyaGoo — Actual Weight and Volumetric Weight
JoyaGoo — Weighing Standards for Each Transportation Service
JoyaGoo — Estimated Billing Weight and Actual Billing Weight

faqs.q: Which divisor should I use in a JoyaGoo shipping calculator?
faqs.a: Use the divisor and conditions for the shipping line currently offered to your destination. With dimensions in centimetres, divide their product by that divisor to obtain kilograms. Check whether the rule applies to your carton size.

faqs.q: How can I estimate the extra freight for one more item?
faqs.a: Quote the existing parcel and the proposed combined parcel with the same destination, line and services. Update the combined measurements and compare the two totals. The difference estimates the added freight.

faqs.q: Why can my final JoyaGoo billing weight exceed the scale weight?
faqs.a: Some routes compare packed scale weight with volumetric weight and bill on the larger result. Check the outer carton measurements, the applicable divisor and any route-specific billing increments in your parcel details.

title: JoyaGoo rehearsal packing: what to keep, what to remove and when to pay
summary: Plan a rehearsal around the decision it will help you make, write a packing request the warehouse can follow, and check the result before dispatch.

sections.heading: Decide what the rehearsal will settle
paragraphs: A rehearsal is most useful when you can finish this sentence before paying for it. “Once I see the packed result, I will decide whether to …” You might be comparing one parcel with two, deciding whether the current box meets a line's size rule, or checking how much space an original shoebox takes up alongside clothing. If you only want to see a closer picture of stitching on the shoes, an item photo addresses that question directly. Packing the shoes with other orders would add a step without giving you the view you need.

JoyaGoo describes rehearsal as a paid service in which you choose stored orders, packing options and a shipping line, then receive an updated packed weight and shipping fee. Its help pages show the service price using different currencies. Read the amount and currency displayed in your own request before submitting. The service charge pays for the warehouse work. Keep it on a separate line from the freight when you assess whether the extra information is worth buying. A result that confirms the first estimate can still answer a worthwhile question.

sections.heading: Choose a stable list of warehouse items
paragraphs: Open the warehouse and make a list of the exact orders you intend to send. Use the reference attached to each warehouse item and a short description such as “blue jacket, medium” or “black trainers, size 42.” Two variants of the same listing can look almost identical in small photos. Checking them individually now saves a difficult conversation later about which item the warehouse was asked to pack. Keep separate any item for which you are still waiting on a measurement or considering a return.

Think about the item that has yet to arrive. If its shape would dictate the entire parcel, such as a rigid bag that cannot be folded, a rehearsal of the remaining goods may tell you little about the final plan. If you would send the available goods independently, a rehearsal of those goods can still inform that decision. Write down which case applies. Later, when looking at a packed weight in your account, you will know exactly which orders that number covers and why you chose them.

sections.heading: Make an explicit decision about the retail box
paragraphs: Take a pair of shoes as an example. The seller's shipping carton, the printed retail shoebox, tissue inside the shoes and the final international carton serve different purposes. A request to “remove box” leaves plenty of room for misunderstanding. If you want the retail box for a gift, name it and identify its item reference. If the packaging itself matters, decide whether a dented corner would bother you. Keeping a retail box and preserving its appearance in transit are separate requirements that may call for different protection.

If you do not want that box, first look at what it contains. Loose laces, spare parts or an accessory pouch can end up in a corner that is easy to miss. Identify what must travel with the item. Where the platform offers a removal option, select it only for the item concerned and explain any exception in the remarks. Ask whether the packing team can carry out a special request when its feasibility is uncertain. Treat removing or discarding packaging as a decision you may be unable to reverse.

sections.heading: Write instructions that two people would interpret the same way
paragraphs: For a mixed parcel, one clear instruction per item works better than an overall request to save space. A sample note could read, “For the black trainers, keep the retail shoebox and spare laces together. For the grey hoodie, remove only the disposable outer shipping bag if appropriate. Keep its tags. Please contact me before discarding any rigid packaging from the remaining item.” Adapt the wording to the available options and references. An example note explains your priorities. Acceptance of a request depends on what the warehouse can do.

Read your note from the packer's side of the table. Could that person point to the object you mean without seeing your shopping cart? Would tightening a strap, folding a brim or placing an item under a heavier box conflict with something you care about? Describe the outcome you need and leave room for a workable method. A structured cap that should keep its shape might need space around its crown. Demanding the smallest possible carton in the same note creates a conflict the packer cannot resolve on your behalf.

sections.heading: Budget for protection where damage would matter
paragraphs: A carton that fits a stack of folded garments presents a different problem from one containing the same garments and a rigid accessory. Draw a rough outline of the largest item on paper and identify the surfaces that cannot take pressure. A hat brim, a framed print or the corners of a presentation box may need clearance. Choosing extra protection is easier when you know which part you are trying to protect. Additional material can increase both the packed dimensions and the scale weight, so include it in your intended configuration.

JoyaGoo publishes a parcel packing standard and lists some optional services separately. Read the offered options on the actual request before assuming that a particular treatment is included. If the visual arrangement matters, check whether the parcel photo service available for your order gives the view you need. A photograph taken after sealing can show the outer box. A view before sealing may show the arrangement at the top. Neither view necessarily shows every layer or the condition of an item buried below another box. Specify your question before purchasing additional images.

sections.heading: Review the revised result while the configuration is still clear
paragraphs: Open the rehearsal record in your personal center and compare it with your original note. Start with the item references, selected route and requested packing. Then review the updated weight, shipping amount and any measured dimensions available. Where a dimension is missing and your decision depends on it, ask for the outer carton measurements. This is particularly important when a line imposes a side-length limit. Knowing the weight alone gives you little help in deciding whether a long, narrow carton satisfies that condition.

Consider a hypothetical result in which the packed box is lighter than you expected, but the price looks much the same. A retail box you chose to protect may still determine the length and width of the outer carton. On a route that uses volumetric billing, reduced scale weight alone may have limited impact. Now compare the cost of keeping that box with the value it has to you. If its condition is central to the purchase, retaining it can be the sensible choice even when removing it would make the parcel cheaper.

sections.heading: Know when a new decision requires new information
paragraphs: If you decide to remove an item after the rehearsal, keep the earlier record as a reference for its original contents. Ask how to change the parcel and whether a further service charge applies before authorizing repacking. A different shipping line may apply a different weight rule even if the carton remains unchanged. A different combination of items can require a different carton even if you keep the line. For each change, identify whether it affects the physical measurements, the pricing rule, or both. That tells you which part of the earlier result you can still use.

When you are ready to submit, match the final parcel record to the version you approved. Check the destination, items and route once more, then read the amount due at the payment step. Save the rehearsal reference with the actual parcel reference so you can explain any later difference. After dispatch, the carrier's own measurements can matter to the eventual billing weight. If you have a question then, send the recorded configuration and the specific figure that changed. A short question about one box and one measurement is much easier to resolve than a request to reconstruct the entire order.

sources.title: JoyaGoo — Estimated Billing Weight and Actual Billing Weight

faqs.q: When should I request JoyaGoo rehearsal packing?
faqs.a: Request it when the items you plan to send are in the warehouse and knowing the packed result would change a decision, such as keeping retail packaging or choosing an eligible shipping line.

faqs.q: How do I ask JoyaGoo to keep one shoebox and remove another?
faqs.a: Identify each warehouse item by reference and distinguish its retail shoebox from disposable outer shipping packaging. Select the relevant options and use the remarks field for the exception. Identify loose accessories that should stay with each pair.

faqs.q: Can I use a rehearsal result after changing my parcel contents?
faqs.a: The recorded measurements describe the original combination and packing. Ask how the new selection will be packed and whether a revised quote or an additional service fee applies before approving the change.

title: JoyaGoo warehouse storage and consolidation: when should you ship?
summary: Use the storage dates on individual warehouse items to decide which purchases can travel together, when to request an extension and when to pay for a submitted parcel.

sources.title: JoyaGoo guidance for purchases made at different times

faqs.q: When do the 90 days of JoyaGoo warehouse storage begin?
faqs.a: JoyaGoo counts free item storage from the change to Stored. Open each warehouse record to check its own date. A later purchase can arrive on a different schedule.

faqs.q: Can I ship JoyaGoo orders placed on different days together?
faqs.a: Yes. Select the stored items you want in the Warehouse section. Check which shipping lines accept that combination at your destination. Items still on their way from the seller can travel in a later parcel.

faqs.q: How long can a submitted JoyaGoo parcel wait for payment?
faqs.a: The warehouse storage policy gives a submitted, unpaid parcel 30 days of free storage. Follow any earlier payment deadline shown for your order or shipping quote. Contact support before a deadline you cannot meet.

sections.heading: Start with the oldest item you still want
paragraphs: Open the Warehouse section of your JoyaGoo account and find the item that has been there longest. Its storage date gives you a practical deadline for planning a combined parcel. A sweatshirt bought on Monday can arrive after a cap bought on Thursday. Sorting your confirmation emails by purchase date would put those two items in the wrong order. For this decision, the useful event is the change to Stored on each warehouse record.

The official storage policy gives an item 90 days of free warehouse storage from that change. It also describes a separate period for a parcel that has been submitted and is waiting for its shipping fee. Those two records answer different questions. The item record tells you how long a particular purchase may occupy the warehouse. The parcel record tells you what still needs to happen to move a particular box. Open the record that matches the action you are considering.

sections.heading: Give each item a job in the parcel
paragraphs: Suppose you have a jacket for an upcoming trip, two shirts for everyday wear and a bag that the seller has yet to send. Write one line for each purchase. Include its warehouse item reference, the variant, whether you have accepted the available photos, the date shown in storage and your reason for waiting. The jacket has a travel date. The shirts have flexibility. The bag has an unconfirmed arrival. That difference will matter more than the order in which you added them to the cart.

Use a description that would let someone else pick out the right item. Two black shirts from one listing might differ only in sleeve length or size. Keep both warehouse references beside those descriptions. When you select the parcel contents, tick the reference as well as reading the thumbnail. If a size still looks uncertain in the photos, mark that issue on the line. The item can stay out of this parcel while you ask about it.

sections.heading: Decide whether waiting changes the outcome
paragraphs: Give an expected arrival a source. A seller who has promised to send an item has given you one kind of information. A domestic courier event recording delivery to the warehouse gives you another. Neither tells you that the item is already available for selection. Check your account again when the warehouse record changes. If the seller has given only a vague estimate, plan the existing parcel using the goods you can actually see.

Now choose a date to decide about the late bag. Work back from the jacket's intended use, allowing time to select a route, pack the parcel and receive it. Use the current delivery estimate shown for your destination and allow for uncertainty. If the remaining days already leave little room, even an inexpensive addition may have a high practical cost. When everything is flexible and ample storage remains, waiting until a specific review date can save the effort of managing two deliveries.

sections.heading: Compare two feasible parcels
paragraphs: On the warehouse page, select a group of stored items and inspect the available shipping options. JoyaGoo's guidance for purchases made at different times says the warehouse provides estimates for packaged weight and volume. Record the destination, selected items, available line and quoted amount together. A lone freight number is difficult to interpret later because changing the contents can change the routes and packaging assumptions behind it.

Try the jacket by itself, then the jacket with the shirts. Look at the change in total freight and at the services offered for each selection. To compare sending two parcels with sending one, you need a quote for the second parcel as well as the first. A cheap quote for sending the jacket alone might leave a costly shipment of shirts behind. Keep all amounts in the same currency and note any packing services included in only one option. Revisit the comparison if the seller eventually delivers a much bulkier bag than you expected.

A combination can look economical until one item's shape changes the box. Shoes that must keep their original box and clothing that can be folded place different demands on packing. Decide which features of the packaging you want retained before comparing quotes. If the box itself is part of a gift, saving freight by removing it would defeat your purpose. Compare the options that would deliver the goods in the condition you actually want.

sections.heading: Check pending decisions before you select the items
paragraphs: Long storage is useful when you are waiting for purchases to arrive. It does little for a seller issue that needs attention now. Read any open messages on the order and examine the pictures of the particular SKU you bought. Look for a missing component, a different colour or quantity, or a measurement that affects your decision. Use the seller's current return or exchange terms and the deadline on the order when deciding how quickly to respond.

For a pair of shoes, for example, a picture of the outside of the box may confirm the label. A separate view of the pair may be needed to settle a question about the colour supplied. Explain the precise point the additional view would answer. If you decide to exchange, leave the item off the parcel selection until its replacement has arrived and you have checked it. You can now reconsider whether the other goods should travel independently.

sections.heading: Extend storage deliberately
paragraphs: When you need more time, open the extension option on the item in your warehouse account. Read the fee, the period offered and the item reference before confirming. JoyaGoo's storage help describes paid extensions. Rely on the amount and revised expiry shown for your own purchase when budgeting. Record the updated date after payment and keep the confirmation with the item reference. Several items arriving weeks apart may each need a different decision.

An extension has a concrete purpose when, for example, you have confirmed the replacement shipment for a jacket and want it to travel with a matching pair of trousers. Compare the cost of extending the trousers with the additional freight of sending separate parcels. If the replacement is still hypothetical, choose a point at which you will reassess. When an extension control is missing or a date is unclear, send the item reference and displayed date to official support while time remains.

sections.heading: Follow the parcel through payment
paragraphs: After selecting your items, review the contents and the delivery address on the parcel you are about to submit. For a flat or shared building, read the address as a courier would read it. Confirm the unit identifier and the recipient information requested by the route. Save the list of contents against the parcel reference. An order split across two boxes can otherwise become surprisingly hard to reconstruct when one box reaches you first.

JoyaGoo's storage policy describes 30 days of free storage for the submitted parcel awaiting freight payment.
